what: Equinor is Norway's state-controlled energy company. It produces oil and gas, mostly from the Norwegian continental shelf, supplies a large share of Europe's natural gas, trades energy, and builds offshore wind.
customers: European utilities and industrial gas buyers, refiners, and power markets.
money: oil and gas from the Norwegian continental shelf
moat: Low-cost Norwegian fields and the pipeline system that delivers gas directly into European markets, a position no other supplier holds.
risks: European gas prices have fallen from their crisis peaks
Norwegian petroleum taxation is very high
Offshore wind projects have had cost overruns industry-wide
Reported net margin is low because of the tax regime
opportunities: Return on invested capital near 30% is among the highest in the industry
Europe's need for non-Russian gas supports long-term demand
A strong balance sheet with cash close to debt
watch: European gas prices and Norwegian production volumes.
